Subject: Intermittent 503s to Hosted API since 9:00AM PT

Hi Michael,

We're seeing a sharp spike in 503 responses from the Hosted API starting at ~09:00 PT this morning. Our error rate on the /v1/generate endpoint jumped from <0.3% to ~18% and many of our production flows are timing out. Sample request IDs we captured: rq_8f3a, rq_8f42, rq_8f8c.

We validated it's coming from the Redwood Hosted endpoint in us-west-2. Can you confirm whether there is an active incident or maintenance window? This is affecting Brightworks billing and order-processing flows — we're seeing queued messages piling up and would like an ETA.

Attaching a small sample of our client-side error logs (referenced in the S3 link if that's easier).

Thanks,
Aisha

Subject: Re: Intermittent 503s to Hosted API since 9:00AM PT

Hi Aisha — thanks for flagging this and for the sample request IDs. We're investigating immediately.

Summary of initial actions:
- I opened INFRA-1248 and started an incident bridge (link below).
- Engineering is checking host-level OOM/eviction signals and the serving runtime's affinity routing to us-west-2.
- We've temporarily enabled regional fallback routing for your tenant to route a subset of traffic to us-west-1 to limit customer impact while we triage.

Can you confirm whether you want us to keep the fallback enabled for the next 2 hours? That will route ~25% of requests away from the impacted pool (we expect lower latency variation, but possible minor model-selection differences).

Status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/BR-20280302-503-wave
JIRA: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-1248

I'll follow up on triage details within the hour.

Forwarding quick triage notes from the bridge:

On Thu, 2 Mar 2028, 09:40 Michael Grant wrote:
> Triage summary (observed at 09:00-09:30 PT):
> - Spike in 503 responses correlated with a KV cache thrash on the us-west-2 serving pool.
> - Simultaneous autoscaler thrash caused short-lived allocation churn; a subset of requests hit nodes that were still warming leading to 503s.
> - Root cause candidate: a regression in the recent cache checkpointing change that delays KV restore during node start.
>
> Mitigations applied:
> 1) Enabled regional fallback for impacted tenants (25% diversion to us-west-1).
> 2) Increased min replica count for us-west-2 pool to reduce allocation churn while we revert the problematic checkpointing flag.
> 3) Rolling restart scheduled for the most impacted host group, with a staggered drain to avoid simultaneous cold starts.
>
> Next steps: engineering to revert checkpointing flag in the canary pool, monitor error rates, and ship a fix to prevent regression in next runtime rollout.

Marissa: please confirm we've captured the correct timeline and post the short update to the status page. Evelyn, can you validate metrics and attach the latency/error graphs?

Date: Thu, 2 Mar 2028 13:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Update — 503 wave resolved; brief postmortem & next steps

Hi Aisha — quick update and next steps from our post-incident work. Apologies again for the disruption this morning.

What happened (summary):
- Between 09:00 and 09:30 PT we observed a rapid increase in 503 responses driven by a KV cache checkpointing regression that increased restore latency during node startups. That, combined with aggressive autoscaler behavior, produced temporary allocation churn and a wave of requests hitting partially-warmed hosts.

What we did:
- Immediately activated a regional fallback to divert a share of traffic to us-west-1 (reduced customer-visible 503s while we triaged).
- Increased min replicas on the us-west-2 pool and staged a rolling restart to avoid simultaneous cold starts.
- Reverted the checkpointing flag in the runtime canary and validated restore latencies — the fix removed the regression.

Current state:
- Error rates returned to baseline by ~12:15 PT. Full checking completed at ~13:00 PT and the rollback remains in place pending a safe fix timeline.

What we are doing next (postmortem):
- Internal RCA and remediation plan drafted (attached: postmortem_draft_v1.pdf).
- We'll harden the checkpoint/restore path and add end-to-end canary checks to prevent similar regressions.
- We're evaluating an autoscaler safety gating change to reduce allocation churn during high restore latencies.

Customer impact & credits:
- We recorded elevated 503 duration for Brightworks from 09:00–12:15 PT. If you'd like, we can propose a targeted service credit for the impacted window and walk that through with your procurement team.

Logs & evidence:
- Incident metrics snapshot attached (incident_metrics_snapshot.png). Full logs and request samples are in the S3 path: s3://redwood-logs/brightworks/2028-03-02/.

If you prefer, we can set a 30-min postmortem review call tomorrow to walk through the timeline and remediation plan.

Thanks for your patience — we'll follow up with a finalized postmortem and timeline for the permanent fix.

Best,
Michael Grant
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
